I will keep my farm in a steady, labor-efficient pattern because I only have a 2-person household and some labor is tied up off-farm. I have 40 years of farming experience, I can irrigate from wells, and I am educated enough to manage inputs carefully, so I will not farm too conservatively but I also will not chase extreme input levels. I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is my core system and the most reliable way for me to use land, water, and machinery efficiently in Quzhou County. I will keep a smaller share in cotton because it still fits my farm, spreads risk, and gives me a cash crop, but it needs more attention, so I will not let it take too much area.

On 15 mu, I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 10 mu, and I will keep 5 mu in cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, solid base fertilization, and three irrigations because I have well water and I want stable tillering, jointing, and grain filling. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and lower tillage intensity, because after wheat harvest I want fast turnaround and labor saving. For cotton, I will use hybrid seed, moderate nitrogen with relatively stronger potassium, and a few more pesticide sprays because cotton is more management-intensive and I need to protect yield. I am aiming for stable, realistic yields rather than the highest possible yields.
